name: Royal Mansour Marrakech
insider_take: This palatial property isn't just a hotel—it's a hand-crafted marvel where traditional Moroccan artisans spent four years creating a living masterpiece in the heart of the medina.
whats_special: Each of the 53 riads is a private three-story sanctuary with its own rooftop terrace, underground tunnels connect guests discreetly throughout the property, and over 1,500 Moroccan craftsmen hand-carved every zellige tile and cedar panel. The hotel sits just steps from Jemaa el-Fnaa square, where snake charmers and storytellers have gathered for centuries.
pro_tip: Book the spa's traditional hammam experience—the marble-clad facility uses centuries-old Moroccan wellness rituals and features a stunning geometric dome that's an artwork in itself.
dont_miss: Sunset at La Grande Table Marocaine on the rooftop with panoramic views of the Atlas Mountains, and exploring the nearby Saadian Tombs—a 16th-century royal necropolis that was sealed for centuries and only rediscovered in 1917.
pros: Extraordinary Moroccan palace architecture with authentic craftsmanship
Private riads with individual pools and terraces
Michelin-starred dining and exceptional culinary experiences
cons: Formal atmosphere may not suit casual travelers
